description: Defines how A.R.I.A. stores, retrieves, ranks, scopes, compresses, expires, and supplies memory to the reasoning system while keeping canonical knowledge, historical experience, user-specific experience, active case state, and conversational context logically separated.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall not attempt to place everything she knows into the language model context. Memory shall be retrieved according to relevance, authority, scope, recency, diagnostic value, and current reasoning state.
rules: Persistent intelligence shall exist outside the language model context window.
The language model receives a selected working set rather than the entire ARIA knowledge system.
Canonical knowledge, learned experience, user-specific experience, case history, and conversation history are distinct memory domains.
Memory retrieval shall preserve provenance.
Memory relevance does not imply truth.
User-specific memory shall remain scoped to the applicable user.
Current case evidence shall normally outrank historical similarity when determining present technical state.
Memory retrieval shall be dynamic as the reasoning state changes.

memory_domains.name: CANONICAL_KNOWLEDGE
memory_domains.description: Validated technical knowledge represented by the knowledge graph, authoritative references, technical relationships, product definitions, procedures, constraints, and engineering rules.

memory_domains.name: EXPERIENCE_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Historical diagnostic experience derived from validated cases and stored through the Experience Ledger.

memory_domains.name: USER_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Contextual historical experience associated with a specific user, including applicable technical history, action performance, evidence patterns, and communication preferences.

memory_domains.name: CASE_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Complete historical record of an individual diagnostic case including observations, evidence, hypotheses, probabilities, routes, actions, outcomes, corrections, and validation.

memory_domains.name: WORKING_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Current compact representation of information required to reason about the active case.

memory_domains.name: CONVERSATIONAL_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Recent conversational content required to understand references, intent, questions, answers, and dialogue continuity.

memory_domains.name: PROCEDURAL_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Reusable knowledge describing how diagnostic, configuration, installation, validation, and corrective actions are performed.

memory_domains.name: TEMPORARY_RETRIEVAL_MEMORY
memory_domains.description: Information retrieved for a specific reasoning operation but not necessarily retained in active working memory after the operation completes.

working_memory.purpose: Maintain the smallest sufficient representation of the active diagnostic state.
rules: Working memory shall represent current state rather than duplicate the entire case history.
Older details may be retrieved from case memory when needed.
Material contradictions shall remain represented until resolved.
Ruled-out hypotheses shall remain summarized sufficiently to prevent unnecessary repetition.
Working memory shall be reconstructable from authoritative case records.

episodic_case_memory.description: Every diagnostic case is an episode that can later be retrieved by technical similarity.
rules: Historical cases shall remain individually retrievable.
Case similarity shall not imply identical cause.
Retrieved cases shall preserve their outcome confidence and learning eligibility.
Low-quality historical cases shall not be presented as equivalent to fully validated cases.
ARIA shall be capable of retrieving both similar successful cases and important counterexamples.

user_memory.description: ARIA shall maintain user-specific experience without cloning the entire global knowledge graph for each user.
rules: The knowledge graph shall not be physically duplicated for each user.
The Experience Ledger shall not be physically duplicated for each user.
User overlays shall reference shared entities and shared case structures.
User-specific aggregates may be materialized for performance.
A user overlay shall modify retrieval and reasoning context without creating a separate technical universe.

steps.name: DEFINE_RETRIEVAL_NEED
steps.description: Determine what information the current reasoning operation requires.

steps.name: SELECT_MEMORY_DOMAINS
steps.description: Determine which memory domains are relevant.

steps.name: APPLY_SCOPE_FILTERS
steps.description: Restrict retrieval according to applicable user, product, manufacturer, case, topology, scope, time, and other context.

steps.name: RETRIEVE_CANDIDATES
steps.description: Retrieve candidate graph nodes, records, documents, cases, experience events, and summaries.

steps.name: RANK_CANDIDATES
steps.description: Rank candidate memories according to relevance and reasoning value.

steps.name: DIVERSIFY
steps.description: Prevent near-duplicate retrieved memories from consuming the working context.

steps.name: AUTHORITY_CHECK
steps.description: Preserve distinction between canonical, empirical, conversational, and uncertain information.

steps.name: COMPRESS
steps.description: Reduce retrieved material into the smallest representation that preserves diagnostically important meaning.

steps.name: ASSEMBLE_WORKING_CONTEXT
steps.description: Construct the information package supplied to the reasoning operation.

retrieval_score.conceptual_formula: retrieval_score = relevance + applicability + authority + diagnostic_value + novelty - redundancy
rules: Exact weights shall remain configurable.
Retrieval scoring shall depend on the reasoning task.
Canonical knowledge may receive higher authority while empirical cases may receive higher contextual similarity.
Contradictory memories may receive increased retrieval value when they challenge the leading hypothesis.

retrieval_modes.name: GRAPH_RETRIEVAL
retrieval_modes.description: Traverse explicit relationships between technical entities.

retrieval_modes.name: SEMANTIC_RETRIEVAL
retrieval_modes.description: Retrieve information based on semantic similarity.

retrieval_modes.name: STRUCTURED_FILTER_RETRIEVAL
retrieval_modes.description: Retrieve records matching explicit structured fields.

retrieval_modes.name: TEMPORAL_RETRIEVAL
retrieval_modes.description: Retrieve information according to time relationships.

retrieval_modes.name: HYBRID_RETRIEVAL
retrieval_modes.description: Combine graph, semantic, structured, user, and temporal retrieval.

rules: Semantic similarity alone shall not determine technical applicability.
Graph relationships alone may be insufficient when terminology differs.
Structured filters shall be used whenever applicable context is known.
Hybrid retrieval should combine complementary retrieval methods when the diagnostic value justifies it.

context_budget.description: ARIA shall treat language-model context as a scarce computational resource.
rules: Context shall be assembled for the current operation rather than permanently loaded.
Large source documents should normally be retrieved in relevant sections rather than injected in full.
Repeated information should be deduplicated before context assembly.
Structured representations should be preferred when they preserve meaning more efficiently than prose.
Critical provenance references shall survive compression.
Compression shall not replace authoritative source records.
A summary shall preserve references to underlying records.
Material uncertainty and contradictions shall survive compression.
Exact values required for calculations shall not be replaced by vague summaries.
Summaries may be regenerated when underlying records change.
Equivalent memories shall not consume context repeatedly.
Duplicate source artifacts shall be identified when practical.
Multiple historical aggregates derived from the same cases shall not be presented as independent evidence.
Shared technical concepts shall be represented once and referenced from multiple contexts.
Deduplication shall preserve meaningful contextual differences.
Current-state memories may become stale after technical changes.
Stable canonical engineering knowledge does not become stale merely because it is old.
Firmware-specific and software-specific knowledge shall preserve version applicability.
User-specific behavioral experience may receive recency weighting.
Superseded information shall remain historically retrievable.
Conflicting memories shall preserve their source and authority.
Canonical documentation and field experience may disagree without either being silently deleted.
Current direct evidence may establish that a device is not behaving according to documented expectation.
Historical majority shall not automatically override an applicable deterministic technical rule.
Material conflicts shall be surfaced to the reasoning engine.
A memory may have multiple applicable scopes.
More specific scope does not automatically imply greater truth.
Retrieval shall favor the most applicable sufficiently reliable scope.
Unknown scope shall reduce applicability confidence.

memory_write_policy.description: Not everything discussed with ARIA becomes persistent memory.
rules: Persistent writes shall identify their target memory domain.
Temporary reasoning shall not silently become permanent learned experience.
Authoritative knowledge writes shall follow knowledge governance.
User-specific experience writes shall follow learning eligibility rules.
Invalidation shall not normally delete historical records.
Invalid memories shall be excluded from current authoritative retrieval unless historical reconstruction requires them.
Derived summaries and aggregates affected by invalidation shall be regenerable.
Memory invalidation shall preserve reason, timestamp, and affected dependencies.

memory_reconstruction.description: ARIA shall be capable of reconstructing what she knew and why she reasoned as she did at an earlier point in a case.

model_context_interface.description: Defines the boundary between ARIA's persistent intelligence and the language model.
rules: The model shall not be the authoritative storage layer.
Model context may be discarded and reconstructed.
The same persistent ARIA memory architecture may support different future language models.
Increasing ARIA's total stored knowledge shall not require proportional growth of the model context window.

example.interpretation: ARIA may possess millions of persistent records while supplying the language model only the small set needed for the current reasoning operation.

semantic_rules.rule: ARIA's memory is not equivalent to the language model context window.
Persistent intelligence shall remain reconstructable independently of any single language-model invocation.
The global knowledge graph and Experience Ledger shall be shared rather than physically replicated for every user.
User-specific intelligence shall be implemented as scoped overlays and relationships referencing shared technical entities and historical cases.
Memory retrieval shall be driven by the current reasoning need.
Semantic similarity shall not substitute for technical applicability.
ARIA shall retrieve counterexamples and contradictory experience when diagnostically valuable.
Working memory shall contain current state, not the complete history of how that state was reached.
Complete historical reasoning shall remain available outside working memory.
Compression shall reduce context size without destroying provenance, uncertainty, contradictions, or calculation-critical values.
Repeated information shall not receive additional authority merely because it appears in multiple retrieved representations.
Memory scope and source authority shall remain explicit.
Historical experience shall influence current reasoning without becoming current-case evidence.
Conversation history shall support continuity but shall not silently become canonical technical knowledge.
ARIA shall preserve the ability to reconstruct what information was available when a historical decision was made.
Memory retrieval performance shall be improved through indexing, materialized aggregates, graph traversal, and scoped retrieval rather than uncontrolled duplication.
A memory may be relevant without being correct; retrieval and authority evaluation are separate operations.
The language model may request memory retrieval but shall not independently fabricate persistent memories.
The memory architecture shall permit ARIA to change language models without losing her accumulated technical experience.
ARIA's effective intelligence shall scale primarily through structured knowledge, experience, retrieval, and reasoning rather than requiring all accumulated knowledge to reside in model weights.
